sb_prompt: WHAT ADVICE OR EXPERIENCE CAN YOU OFFER TO A PARENT ON HOW TO HELP A SON OR DAUGHTER CHOOSE A COLLEGE TO ATTEND?
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hey there.
ParticipantA: Sorry, was the right number?
ParticipantB: Yeah, that's me. How are you?
ParticipantA: Pretty good. You too?
ParticipantB: Yeah, I'm good. Just busy with the store today.
ParticipantA: Oh, sorry, I thought you said you were a manager or something.
ParticipantB: Ah, right, I'm at the grocery store. Managing it, yeah.
ParticipantA: Oh, cool. That's awesome. I'm actually in retail too, just a bit younger, maybe 26?
ParticipantB: Oh, wow, really? That's young. I'm 44, so I can see you're in my late 20s probably.
ParticipantA: Yeah, just graduated college last year, trying to figure things out.
ParticipantB: Yeah, me too. Actually, that's what I was hoping to talk about.
ParticipantA: Oh? Yeah, sure.
ParticipantB: So, if a parent calls you, asking about helping their kid pick a college, what do you say?
ParticipantA: Well, honestly, it's pretty straightforward. You just ask them what they actually want to do.
ParticipantB: Oh, really?
ParticipantA: Like, do they want to be a mechanic or an accountant? If they don't even like math, don't send them to business school.
ParticipantB: That's true. My son, he went to a big state school right here, and he was there for two years.
ParticipantA: Oh? How was it?
ParticipantB: Well, he didn't really like it. He said the classes were too easy, and he was bored.
ParticipantA: That's a problem.
ParticipantB: Yeah, he just wanted to learn stuff, not sit there and read the same textbook for two years. So he transferred.
ParticipantA: That makes sense. I know this guy, his uncle, went to a place way out of state because his parents wanted him to.
ParticipantB: Oh?
ParticipantA: But he hated it. He said he was miserable. Had to drop out after a semester.
ParticipantB: That's rough.
ParticipantA: Yeah, it was a disaster. So now we always ask, "What do you like?" instead of "Where can we get you in?"
ParticipantB: I agree with that. My son, when he transferred, he actually found a program he loved.
ParticipantA: Really? That's great.
ParticipantB: Yeah, he's doing great now. He's studying graphic design. He said, "Dad, I need to be somewhere creative."
ParticipantA: Oh, wow. That's different.
ParticipantB: Yeah, so my advice is, find the thing they actually enjoy. Don't force them into a pre-med track if they draw all day.
ParticipantA: Exactly. That's what my uncle said about me. He said, "You love cars, son, go to the trade school, not the liberal arts place."
ParticipantB: So you didn't?
ParticipantA: No, I listened. Went to a community college, then transferred to a tech school for automotive engineering.
ParticipantB: That's smart.
ParticipantA: Yeah, I'm actually a manager at the grocery store now, running a shift. Making good money, doing what I like.
ParticipantB: That's awesome. I'm proud of him too. He's doing well.
ParticipantA: So, if I were a parent, I'd tell them to just ask the kid what they like first.
ParticipantB: Yeah, that's exactly it. Passion comes first. The school is just the tool to get there.
ParticipantA: Makes sense. Don't waste money on a degree they hate.
ParticipantB: Right.
ParticipantA: So, that's my two cents.
ParticipantB: Yeah, that's pretty good advice. Thanks for sharing.
ParticipantA: No problem. Good luck with your son.
ParticipantB: You too. Take care.
ParticipantA: Bye.
ParticipantB: Bye.
